Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Work & responsibility

civil servant noun

also public servant, government employee, civil service, functionary, bureaucrat

classical

Liv. 1.8.3
Levi–Bini p. 33

appāritor, appāritōris m.

noun, third declension

a public servant

Lewis & Short: a public servant, the paid staff of the magistrates (clerks, lictors, messengers, heralds). Unlike the magistrates, they were salaried and stayed on from year to year, as a civil service does. Levi and Bini give it for a junior state employee (p. 33).

Other words

  • scrība, scrībae m. — a public clerk

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.183; Traupman 292

    The clerks who kept the public accounts and records, a respected order (Cic. Verr. 2.3.183; Lewis & Short). Traupman’s word for a clerk.

Examples

  • Est vērō honestus, quod eōrum hominum fideī tabulae pūblicae perīculaque magistrātuum committuntur.

    It is indeed a respected order, for the public accounts and the magistrates’ liabilities are entrusted to these men’s honesty.Cic. Verr. 2.3.183

See also official, office, government.
